source_text:
Ταῦτα, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐμαυτῷ ἐπιτρέψας γράφω ὑμῖν περὶ τῆς δικαιοσύνης, ἀλλ’ ἐπεὶ ὑμεῖς προεπεκαλέσασθέ με.
οὔτε γὰρ ἐγὼ οὔτε ἄλλος ὅμοιος ἐμοὶ δύναται κατακολουθῆσαι τῇ σοφίᾳ τοῦ μακαρίου καὶ ἐνδόξου Παύλου, ὃς γενόμενος ἐν ὑμῖν κατὰ πρόσωπον τῶν τότε ἀνθρώπων ἐδίδαξεν ἀκριβῶς καὶ βεβαίως τὸν περὶ ἀληθείας λόγον, ὃς καὶ ἀπὼν ὑμῖν ἔγραψεν ἐπιστολάς, εἰς ἃς ἐὰν ἐγκύπτητε, δυνηθήσεσθε οἰκοδομεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν δοθεῖσαν ὑμῖν πίστιν:
ἥτις ἐστὶν μήτηρ πάντων ἡμῶν, ἐπακολουθούσης τῆς ἐλπίδος, προαγούσης τῆς ἀγάπης τῆς εἰς θεὸν καὶ Χριστὸν καὶ εἰς τὸν πλησίον. ἐὰν γάρ τις τούτων ἐντὸς ᾖ, πεπλήρωκεν ἐντολὴν δικαιοσύνης: ὁ γὰρ ἔχων ἀγάπην μακράν ἐστιν πάσης ἁμαρτίας.
thought_title: Paul's wisdom and the faith that fulfills righteousness
orientation: Polycarp is explaining why he writes about righteousness only because the Philippians asked him to, since no one can match the wisdom of the apostle Paul, who taught them in person and by letter.
pass_a_gloss: These things, brothers, I write to you about righteousness not having permitted myself, but because you yourselves called me forth. For neither I nor another like me is able to follow closely the wisdom of the blessed and glorious Paul, who, having been among you in the presence of the people of that time, taught accurately and firmly the word about truth, who also, being absent, wrote letters to you, into which if you look closely, you will be able to be built up into the faith given to you: which is mother of all of us, hope following, love going before, love toward God and Christ and toward the neighbor. For if anyone is within these things, he has fulfilled the commandment of righteousness: for the one having love is far from every sin.

choices.why: The compound verb with προ- indicates prior initiative by the Philippians; 'called me forth' preserves the sense of summoning to a task rather than merely asking.
The κατα- prefix intensifies the following; 'follow closely' captures the sense of tracking or keeping pace with Paul's wisdom.
The verb means to stoop down and peer into something, suggesting attentive study of the letters; 'look closely into' preserves that nuance.
The passive infinitive conveys being edified or constructed spiritually; 'be built up' is the standard rendering and keeps the architectural metaphor.

choices.term: ἐπακολουθούσης τῆς ἐλπίδος, προαγούσης τῆς ἀγάπης
choices.why: The genitive absolutes describe hope and love as accompanying the faith; 'following' and 'going before' preserve the directional imagery of the participles.
rejected: with hope following and love leading

choices.why: The phrase means to be inside the sphere of faith, hope, and love; 'within these things' keeps the spatial metaphor of being encompassed by them.

pass_b_english: Brothers and sisters, I am not writing to you about righteousness because I decided to on my own. You yourselves asked me to write.

For neither I nor anyone like me can follow closely the wisdom of the blessed and glorious Paul. When he was among you, he stood before the people of that time and taught the word of truth accurately and firmly. And when he was away, he wrote you letters. If you look closely into them, you will be able to be built up in the faith that was given to you.

That faith is the mother of us all. Hope follows after it, and love goes before it: love toward God and Christ and toward the neighbor. For if anyone lives within these things, that person has fulfilled the commandment of righteousness. The one who has love is far from all sin.

polish.changed: I broke the long opening sentence into clearer units, made the implied subject of the faith explicit, and turned the final conditional into a more natural modern statement while preserving every claim and scriptural reference.

problems.why: Greek 'tois tote' likely means 'those then present,' not a generic 'people of that time.'
problems.fix: Render: 'the people who were there at that time.'

edits.old: he stood before the people of that time
edits.new: he stood before the people who were there at that time

fixed: Changed 'the people of that time' to 'the people who were there at that time' to reflect the Greek 'τῶν τότε ἀνθρώπων' meaning those then present, not a generic group.
